label: CRS418-8P-8G-2S+5axQ2axQ-RM
description: MikroTik CRS418-8P-8G-2S+5axQ2axQ-RM (CRS418-8P-8G-2S+5axQ2axQ-RM) — 17x 1G RJ45, 2x 10G SFP+, Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz + 5 GHz. ARM 64bit 4-core IPQ-8072A.

poe.note: Total output power 150 W, PoE-out ports Ether9-Ether16 (802.3af/at, 8 x 1G ports with PoE-out; each port can also be set to 24 V passive PoE). Ether1-Ether8 and the Ether17 management port do not source power.

notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table (https://mikrotik.com/product/crs418_8p_8g_2s_wifi, HTTP 200, 448,215 B, read 2026-11-21): "10/100/1000 Ethernet ports: 17", "Number of 1G Ethernet ports with PoE-out: 8", "PoE-out ports: Ether9-Ether16", "PoE out: 802.3af/at", "Total output power: 150", "SFP+ ports: 2", plus the marketing row "8x PoE Output ports (802.3af/at and 24V Passive PoE Output) \u2014 up to 150 W total output". A 24 V passive mode is selectable per port but 802.3at is the negotiated standard the engine models, so the ports are classed PoE+ (the row's own 0.56 A high-voltage limit is per port, 30 W at 54 V). Max power consumption 227 W with attachments fitted, 43 W without. Same 8-of-17 split as the non-WiFi CRS418-8P-8G-2S+RM: the "8P" names the PoE block, not the first eight ports. This row was imported with `poe-pse` and no per-port flags, so the engine's switch inference lit all seventeen copper sockets as 15.4 W PSEs; test/crs418-wifi-poe.test.js is the guard.
